Diagnosis on the unedited model: with thinking on it almost never emits </think> (29/32 example problems ran to a 16k cap in "Wait, ..." loops; 2/32 correct vs 13/32 with thinking off). Component A: a read vector (ridge solve on bucket-mean MLP activations) that is ~+1.5 logits early in thinking and ramps to ~+12 with thinking length, and ~-3 to -4 in answer / no-thinking phases (validated on held-out unedited activations, math and general prompts), written along a minimum-norm direction that raises only the </think> logit (zero effect on other special tokens and main newline competitors). Expected: thinking ends typically within ~600-1500 tokens and the model answers; this is an analytic estimate from summary statistics, not a measurement. SUMMARY — rank-2 LoRA on model.layers.23.mlp.down_proj (adapter.npz), built in closed form, never run.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT FIRST: under the rules I did not generate with, or otherwise evaluate, the edited model. Everything below about what the adapter *will do* is a prediction from measurements on the unedited model (its generations, its activations, its weights). I have no measured accuracy for the adapter. No gradients, optimizers or iterative fitting were used; the adapter comes from two regularised least-squares solves and two constrained minimum-norm solves.

1. What is wrong with the unedited model (measured)
- On 32 example problems with thinking on (16,384-token cap), the model almost never leaves its thinking block: 29/32 ran to the cap without ever emitting </think>, mostly inside repetitive "Wait, ..." self-doubt loops. Accuracy 2/32. The same 32 problems with thinking off (6,000-token cap): 13/32.
- The "Wait" spiral is a marker of failure in every phase, not only in thinking. With thinking forced short (28 problems): answers without "Wait" 9/11 correct, answers containing "Wait" 0/17 (16 hit the cap). Thinking off: no "Wait" 10/16 correct, with "Wait" 3/16. This is correlational (harder problems trigger more doubt), so it shows the spiral is unproductive, not that removing the word fixes the reasoning.
- Internally, </think> is typically ~12 logits below the top token at paragraph breaks during thinking (median 11.7–12.6, 5th percentile ~8), and never gets closer as thinking gets longer. The onset of a "Wait" is a close call (it wins by a median 0.2–0.7 logits, 95th percentile <=1.5), but once a loop is entrenched (>5,000 tokens) it wins by ~10 logits.

2. The edit
Only the last layer's MLP output projection is changed, so the edit adds a vector directly to the final residual stream as a linear function of that layer's 3,584-d MLP hidden activation; nothing upstream changes. ||dW||_F = 8.93 = 0.54 x ||W||_F (limit 5x).
